latest_publication.title: How to automate supplier statement reconciliation without hiding exceptions
latest_publication.target_client_type: UK SMEs with finance or operations teams that manually reconcile supplier statements against accounting records and supporting documents
latest_publication.industry_or_operating_context: Broader SME finance operations, accounts payable controls, supplier records and exception handling
latest_publication.primary_buyer_problem: Teams spend time checking every supplier statement line manually even though most lines follow repeatable matching rules, while missing invoices, credits, duplicate references and disputed balances need focused review.
latest_publication.primary_search_intent: Understand how to automate supplier statement reconciliation while keeping unmatched or unsupported items visible for human review.
latest_publication.trend_or_durable_demand: Durable operational demand supported by current HMRC record-keeping requirements. Supplier invoices, credit notes and related accounting records remain evidence businesses need to retain, so reconciliation automation should expose missing evidence rather than manufacture or suppress it.
latest_publication.evidence_source_and_date: GOV.UK Charge, reclaim and record VAT: Keeping VAT records, checked 10 August 2026; HMRC Compliance Handbook CH12200, updated 24 July 2026 and checked 10 August 2026.
latest_publication.existing_article_gap: The site covered invoice intake and approval plus Shopify payout reconciliation, but not supplier statement reconciliation as a separate downstream control over supplier balances, missing documents, credits and duplicate postings.

comparison_against_previous_12.why_meaningfully_distinct: This article reconciles supplier statements against accounting records and supporting evidence after transactions have already entered the business. It does not control invoice approval, reconcile ecommerce payment settlements or decide integration architecture.

latest_publication.original_editorial_asset: A three-way supplier statement reconciliation model supported by a five-row match-and-exception table covering clean matches, missing transactions, value mismatches, missing credits and duplicate risk.
latest_publication.first_hand_contribution_or_limits: Uses Henry Oliver's operating, data-control and automation perspective without claiming specialist accounting advice or invented client results.
latest_publication.proof_points_used_recently: The 200,000-SKU and eight-hours-to-two-minutes proof points were not reused.
